ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A uniform magnetic field of magnitude, $0.50 \, \mathrm{T}$, lies on the $x$-$y$ plane making a $60^\circ$ angle with the $x$-axis. When a $1.2 \, \mu\mathrm{C}$ point charge moves in the $+y$ direction, it experiences a force of magnitude, $3.0 \, \mu\mathrm{N}$. What is the speed of the charged particle?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows x- and y-axes, with +x to the right and +y upward. The magnetic field lines labeled B lie in the x-y plane and point upward to the right. The angle marked between the magnetic field direction and the +x-axis is 60°. Reasoning: The particle velocity is given as being in the +y direction, which is 90° from the +x-axis. Since B is 60° above the +x-axis, the angle between v and B is 90° - 60° = 30°. Use the magnetic force magnitude formula F = |q| v B sin(theta). Given F = 3.0 μN = 3.0e-6 N, q = 1.2 μC = 1.2e-6 C, B = 0.50 T, and sin(30°) = 0.5. Solving gives v = F / (q B sin(theta)) = (3.0e-6) / ((1.2e-6)(0.50)(0.5)) = (3.0e-6) / (3.0e-7) = 10 m/s.

method.method_draft: Resolve the magnetic field into components relative to the particle velocity. Since the charge moves in the +y direction, the component of B parallel to y produces no magnetic force; only the x-component of B is perpendicular to v and contributes. From the diagram/text, B is 60° above +x, so B_x = B cos 60° = 0.50 × 0.5 = 0.25 T. Read q = 1.2 μC and F = 3.0 μN from the text. Use F = |q| v B_perp with B_perp = B_x, so v = F/(q B_x) = 3.0×10^-6 / [(1.2×10^-6)(0.25)] = 10 m/s.
